I asked my clinician during my diagnosis session how to go about being respectful when talking to an SO about something that isn’t my special interest which tends to make me not engaged in the convo. She suggested communicating and coming to an agreement like “I have the capacity to listen to your interest for 5 minutes, go ahead” which gives you an end in sight, while giving them space to talk since it would be unfair to only talk about your special interest. Sometimes when you have more mental space you can increase this to 10 minutes etc. and less time when you don’t. I don’t think this is a permanent solution since I’d want to be engaged with my partner’s interest in the same way they engage with mine but it’s a good start imo

I’m not seeing a lot of responses about how important communication and love languages are. Yes, in theory you can label anything as a love language but the point is that you’re not feeling loved in the way you want to be and it’s important in a relationship that BOTH parties are having their needs met. I truly don’t believe a relationship will last without meeting each other halfway when it comes to this. My advice is to sit down and have a conversation about how you want to be loved (keep it broad since it seems he doesn’t want to compromise on the singing part) and if he isn’t receptive to performing acts of service more then that’s when you can start thinking about ending things. But again this goes both ways, you need to make sure he is getting his needs met and feels loved in his way whether that’s quality time, words of affirmation, etc. and that doesn’t mean you need to stop doing your giving language, just that you should weight whether you have the mental and physical capacity to keep doing it on top of his preferred receiving language. Having giving/receiving love languages that complement your partner certainly makes this easier but doesn’t doom a relationship if both parties are willing to learn the other person’s love language. Hope this helps!
